# Into R: a first look with DESeq2 {#sec-into-r}

`RNApipe` stops at `{runName}_tximport.rds`. This chapter shows how to pick
it up in R and take the first steps of a differential expression analysis
with **DESeq2**. It's an introduction, not a full statistics course. The
[DESeq2 vignette](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html)
is the reference.

::: {.callout-note}
With the 100 k-read test data, the results won't be biologically
meaningful; there are far too few reads. Use it to learn the steps, then run
the same code on a real dataset.
:::

## Setup

Run R either on Longleaf (OnDemand RStudio, or `module load r/4.4.0` then `R`)
or on your laptop after copying the RDS, the copied samplesheet and the GTF.

```r
## install once
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", "tximport", "tximeta", "rtracklayer", "apeglm"))
```

There are two ways in. **Option A** uses the `_tximport.rds` that RNApipe
writes. **Option B** skips it and reads the Salmon folders with **tximeta**
([why](tximport.qmd#tximeta)). Both end in the same `dds` object; everything
from step 4 on is identical.

## Option A: start from the tximport RDS

### 1. Load the object and sample information

```r
library(DESeq2)

txi <- readRDS("output/quant/IMGL_iMGL_WT_1_tximport.rds")
ss  <- read.delim("output/IMGL_iMGL_WT_1_RNApipeSamplesheet.txt",
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                  na.strings = "")      # keep the word "NA" (no treatment) as text

## the current txImporter.R leaves sample names as NA; fix them (order = samplesheet order)
for (m in c("counts", "abundance", "length")) colnames(txi[[m]]) <- ss$sn

dim(txi$counts)          # genes x samples
head(txi$counts)
```

### 2. Describe the samples

DESeq2 needs a table with one row per sample (in the **same order** as the
columns of the matrices) and the variables you want to compare.

```r
coldata <- data.frame(
  row.names = ss$sn,
  condition = factor(paste(ss$Treatment, ss$Time, sep = "_")),
  rep       = factor(ss$Bio_Rep)
)
coldata$condition <- relevel(coldata$condition, ref = "NA_00h")   # the control
coldata
stopifnot(identical(rownames(coldata), colnames(txi$counts)))
```

### 3. Build the DESeq2 object

```r
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromTximport(txi, colData = coldata, design = ~ condition)

## drop genes with almost no reads (speeds things up, doesn't change results much)
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 2
dds  <- dds[keep, ]
```

`DESeqDataSetFromTximport` takes the counts (rounded to whole numbers) and
uses `txi$length` as a per-gene, per-sample offset ([tximport](tximport.qmd)).

## Option B: start from tximeta {#option-b-start-from-tximeta}

```r
library(tximeta)
library(DESeq2)

ss <- read.delim("output/IMGL_iMGL_WT_1_RNApipeSamplesheet.txt",
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")
coldata <- data.frame(
  files     = file.path("output/quant", ss$sn, "quant.sf"),
  names     = ss$sn,
  condition = factor(paste(ss$Treatment, ss$Time, sep = "_")),
  rep       = factor(ss$Bio_Rep)
)
coldata$condition <- relevel(coldata$condition, ref = "NA_00h")

se  <- tximeta(coldata)          # see the tximeta section if it says the index is unknown
gse <- summarizeToGene(se)
dds <- DESeqDataSet(gse, design = ~ condition)
dds <- dds[rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 2, ]
```

A bonus of this route: `rowRanges(dds)` holds each gene's coordinates and,
for GENCODE, its symbol (`mcols(gse)$gene_name` when available), so step 6
below needs no GTF.

## 4. Look before you test: PCA

```r
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = TRUE)        # variance-stabilised values for plotting
plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = "condition")
```

Replicates of a condition should sit near each other. If a sample sits with
the wrong group, check the samplesheet before anything else.

## 5. Test

```r
dds <- DESeq(dds)
resultsNames(dds)                     # e.g. "condition_Ab_24h_vs_NA_00h"
res <- results(dds, name = "condition_Ab_24h_vs_NA_00h", alpha = 0.05)
summary(res)

## shrink fold changes for ranking and plotting
resLFC <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = "condition_Ab_24h_vs_NA_00h", type = "apeglm")
plotMA(resLFC, ylim = c(-5, 5))
```

| Column of `res` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `baseMean` | Average normalised count across all samples |
| `log2FoldChange` | log2(treated / control): 1 = doubled, −1 = halved |
| `lfcSE` | Its standard error |
| `pvalue` | Raw p-value |
| `padj` | **Adjusted p-value** (Benjamini–Hochberg). Use this one; `NA` means the gene was filtered out (too low or an outlier) |

## 6. Add gene names and save

```r
gtf   <- rtracklayer::import("gencode.v49.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf")
genes <- unique(as.data.frame(gtf[gtf$type == "gene"])[, c("gene_id", "gene_name", "gene_type")])

out <- as.data.frame(resLFC)
out$gene_id <- rownames(out)
out <- merge(genes, out, by = "gene_id")
out <- out[order(out$padj), ]
write.csv(out, "DE_Ab24h_vs_ctrl.csv", row.names = FALSE)
head(out[, c("gene_name", "log2FoldChange", "padj")], 20)
```

## Where to go next

- **Normalised counts** for plotting one gene: `plotCounts(dds, gene = "ENSG...", intgroup = "condition")`.
- **Batch or paired designs**: `design = ~ rep + condition` when replicates
  were processed in batches.
- **Gene-set enrichment** (fgsea, clusterProfiler) on the ranked list.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Check your understanding

1. Why must the rows of `coldata` be in the same order as the columns of
   `txi$counts`?
2. A gene has `log2FoldChange = 2` and `padj = 0.3`. How do you describe it?
3. Why do we look at the PCA before running `results()`?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Answers

1. DESeq2 matches them by position. If they're out of order, each sample's
   counts get the wrong condition label, and every result is wrong.
2. It looks 4× higher in the treated samples, but the evidence isn't strong
   enough to call it differentially expressed at the usual cut-off (padj < 0.05).
3. To catch mislabelled samples, outliers or batch effects that would distort
   the test.
:::
:::
